title: Prune degenerate shrink lines by non-maximum suppression
body:
Add prune_shrink_lines, which ranks lines by the FTLE integrated along each and keeps only non-dominated candidates. A line is dropped when it lies inside a tube of radius window_m/2 around a stronger line and its new length outside that tube is less than window_m. Whole lines are kept or dropped as units. The only parameter is window_m, the resolution passed to ftle_ridge_seeds, giving the tube radius and minimum new length.

hyperbolic_lcs now runs the pruning step after shrink_lines, always, so its returned dataset has no all-NaN rows, carries ftle_mean and length_m, and its line labels are seed indices that survived. To get the unpruned set, call ftle_ridge_seeds and shrink_lines by hand with the same parameters and leave out prune_shrink_lines.

On the Cabo Verde example with window_m=30 km, 53 seeds were traced to 38 lines (15 untraceable). Pruning kept 23 lines, removing bundles of near-identical curves along ridges while keeping genuinely separate lines that run together for part of their length. The plan moves to plans/done/.

prune_shrink_lines takes lines as its only positional argument and ftle by keyword, optional; without it the ranking is arc length alone. The step is written over xarray objects, with coverage a pairwise dot-product test on the unit sphere. Prose no longer counts what it lists, and AGENTS.md carries both rules. The changelog section is named 2026.8.27.1 for the release.

title: Allow arbitrary grid-point structure on the auxiliary stencil
body:
The auxiliary stencil differences $\nabla F$ across a grid point's own four arms
and never against another grid point, so nothing in the diagnostic chain needs
the grid points to lie on a mesh. This adds the pair that says so, and carries
the relaxation all the way through the tensor-line layer.

Closes #20. Step 1 of the three-step order in the issue's comment; the exp/log
arm placement (step 2) and the ambient $3\times3$ interpolation of $C$ (step 3)
are untouched.

## What is new

**`UnstructuredAuxiliarySeedGrid` / `UnstructuredAuxiliaryFlowMap`**, built with

```python
seed = UnstructuredAuxiliarySeedGrid.from_points(lon=track_lon, lat=track_lat)
```

An `xr.DataArray` keeps its own dims, so a curvilinear mesh stays a mesh and its
FTLE still plots as a field; a plain 1-D array lands on a `grid_point` dim. The
pair subclasses `Auxiliary*` rather than restating the arm differencing, because
that differencing is measurably layout-free: the same points on `(i, j)` and on
one flat dim give bitwise-identical $\nabla F$, $C$, eigenpairs and FTLE.

**An interpolation seam, `FlowMap._interpolator`.** Both `FlowMap.image` and
`shrink_lines` read a field between grid points, and both were written against
two monotonic axes. They now share one abstract method, answered by bilinear
interpolation along the axes for the rectilinear pairs and by linear
interpolation on a Delaunay triangulation for the unstructured one. `image` was
rewritten onto it and keeps its outer-product and pointwise indexer semantics.

**`src/lcs_parcels/_spatial.py`**, the one module that imports SciPy: the sphere
the package measures on, the two interpolator builders, and the neighbourhood
maximum below. The deferred-import note in `architecture.md` named this module's
own precondition ("until something else needs that module to exist"), and this
is it.

## What breaks

`ftle_ridge_seeds` takes a *field*, not a flow map, so it cannot dispatch on the
layout and a rolling `(i, j)` window would have to sniff the field for axes.
It now picks a seed when its FTLE is the maximum over every grid point within
`window_m / 2` of it along the great circle, through a k-d tree in Earth-centred
Cartesian metres. One rule, either layout, no grid resolution in it.

- **The seed set differs for the same call**, silently. On a uniform
  mid-latitude grid, by a handful of peaks either way. On a domain spanning
  20 N to 75 N the old rule resolved `window_m` against one *median* cell size,
  degenerated to a single cell north of 50 N, and returned 9.3 times as many
  seeds there; below 40 N the two agree exactly.
- **`window_cells_i`, `window_cells_j`, `grid_spacing_i_m` and
  `grid_spacing_j_m` are gone** from the returned `attrs`. Reading one raises
  `KeyError`.
- **`min_seed_separation_m` is exactly `window_m / 2`** and no longer grid-derived.
  The Cabo Verde example goes 16871.8 → 15000.0.
- **The narrow-window `UserWarning` fires on a different condition**, "most grid
  points have no neighbour inside the radius" rather than "fewer than three
  cells".

Rewriting `image` onto the seam changes two more things, both of them
improvements, and both in `CHANGELOG.md` as well:

- On a non-monotonic `lon_grid` axis it now **raises** the same SciPy
  `ValueError` `shrink_lines` does, instead of reading the axis as if it were
  sorted and returning `NaN` or a value interpolated between the wrong two grid
  points.
- Its returned `lon_0`/`lat_0` coords are **broadcast against each other**, so
  every returned position is paired with the reference position it came from.
  Two indexers on different dims used to give a 1-D `lon_0` beside a 2-D `lon`.

`EARTH_RADIUS_M` moved to `lcs_parcels._spatial` with the queries that need it.
It is not exported from the package root and never was, and no test imported it
from `grids`, but the move is announced.

`CHANGELOG.md` carries every one of these with what to write instead.

## Measurements

- The ridge rule was validated bit-for-bit against an all-pairs great-circle
  brute force on a regular grid, a point cloud and a converging-meridian grid at
  80 N, each with 15% NaN.
- `min_seed_separation_m` is provably exact, not empirically safe: the ball test
  is symmetric, so two seeds inside the radius would have to be equal-valued.
  Measured tightness on a 20–75 N band at `window_m = 15_000`: the closest pair
  sits 12 m beyond the 7500 m bound.
- Cost: about 2.4 s against 0.22 s on a million grid points at a 15 km radius,
  most of it assembling neighbour lists. Noted in `numerics.md` beside #11.
- Bilinear and barycentric interpolation agree exactly at grid nodes and differ
  by 0.78% of the field range between them, which is why both are kept rather
  than the scattered one used everywhere.

## Example

`examples/cabo_verde_unstructured` runs the whole chain over 10 000 points that
are not a grid, 4 000 spread over the release box and 6 000 concentrated on the
eddy field (9.4 km against 2.8 km mean spacing, both measured over the same 1 km
arms). It shades the FTLE over the point set's own Delaunay triangulation,
masking the triangles a lost grid point touches, extracts both LCS families, and
carries them through five daily horizons with `FlowMap.image`.

`example_grid_pset` gains a third section, and `cabo_verde_lcs` and
`cabo_verde_lcs_evolution` were re-executed for the new seed sets.

## Deliberately not done

`plans/publish-to-pypi.md` still describes the four deleted `attrs` keys and the
three-cell warning under "As built" for its PR 2. That section is a past-tense
record of what that PR shipped, so it is left alone; the plan is fully
implemented and archiving it under `plans/done/` is a separate call.

## Checks

`pixi run lint`, `pixi run test-cov` (385 tests, 100% coverage),
`pixi run -e examples pytest tests/test_examples.py` and
`pixi run -e docs docs-build` all pass, as does `twine check --strict`.

Reviewed by a four-lens adversarial pass (correctness, prose against `AGENTS.md`,
documentation consistency, scope) with every finding independently refuted or
confirmed; 22 survived and all 22 are applied. Two were real defects in `image`:
the returned `lat` was built from the caller's `lon_0` and so inherited its
attributes, and `position`, the dim `image` builds internally, was missing from
the reserved set a caller's grid dims are checked against. Both now have tests.

title: Wrap the flow-map repr, link the repository, add CITATION.cff
body:
The flow-map repr ran to 101 columns on one line, which scrolls sideways in a
Markdown code block on GitHub and on PyPI wherever it is pasted. It is now two
lines: the grid and its extent, then `t0` and `T` hanging under the first
field. No field was dropped and nothing was rounded. The indent is measured
from the class name, so `AuxiliaryFlowMap` aligns as well. The `SeedGrid` repr
already fitted at 65 columns and is unchanged, and its test still guards that.

```pycon
>>> print(flowmap)
<NeighborFlowMap 6x5 grid, lon -25.00..-20.00, lat 15.00..20.00,
                 t0 2020-01-01T00:00:00, T +7.0 days>
```

The two committed notebooks that print a flow map had the affected output
lines rewrapped in place rather than being re-executed, so the diff is the four
lines that changed and none of the timestamp, UUID and base64-PNG churn that
issue #42 measured. The rewrapped output was checked against a real run of
`example_grid_pset` and is byte-identical to it.

Every page of the documentation site now carries a link to the repository,
through alabaster's sidebar: a GitHub button plus plain "Source on GitHub" and
"Issues" links, which work when the button's third-party iframe does not. The
README names the repository too, for the reader who arrives on PyPI.

`CITATION.cff` is what GitHub reads for its "Cite this repository" widget and
what Zenodo reads for the author list of an archived release. Without it Zenodo
derives authors from the GitHub contributors API and stores each whole display
name as a family name with no ORCID. It carries no `version` or `date-released`:
Zenodo drops both, and the git tag stays the only place a version is written.
The `build` CI job validates the file, because Zenodo fails a release outright
rather than falling back when it cannot parse it.

The README drops the sentence about keyword-only lon/lat pairs. The example
above it already shows the signature.

## What was checked

- `pixi run lint`, `pixi run test-cov` (312 passed, 100% coverage), and
  `pixi run -e docs docs-build` all pass. The GitHub links were confirmed in the
  rendered sidebar of `api.html`, not only on the home page.
- `twine check --strict` passes on both distributions, so the README still
  renders on PyPI.
- `CITATION.cff` validates with `cffconvert` 2.0.0 and against the official CFF
  1.2.0 schema. `cffconvert -f apalike` renders
  `Owusu Adjei H., Rath W. LCS-Parcels`.
- Alabaster's option names were read off the installed 1.0.0 theme rather than
  from memory. `github_banner` is deliberately unset: that key is the corner
  ribbon, and any value other than the literal `"false"` turns it on.

## Zenodo, for the badge follow-up

Verified against the `zenodo-rdm` source and the current help pages, not from
memory:

- A `.zenodo.json` would disable `CITATION.cff` completely. There is no merge
  and no warning, so this repository should keep the one file and not add the
  other.
- Both files are read from the repository root **at the release tag**. Adding a
  file to `main` after tagging does nothing for that release.
- Zenodo maps `title`, `abstract`, `authors`, `keywords`, `license` and
  `message` and silently drops the rest, `version` and `type` included, despite
  Zenodo's own example page listing them.
- Because a CFF is present, the record's publication date becomes the date
  Zenodo processes the release rather than the GitHub release date, and the
  record publisher is forced to the literal `Zenodo`.
- Both authors carry an ORCID, which is the main reason to have a CFF at all:
  the no-metadata default attaches none. Zenodo validates the check digit, so an
  invalid one fails the release; both were verified before being committed.

`#43` stays open for the badge, which needs the concept DOI that only exists
once Zenodo has archived a first release.

Note on the changelog: the new section is dated `2026.8.8.1`. If the release is
tagged on another day, the heading moves with the tag.

Closes #41

title: Track non-executed notebooks and execute at docs build time
body:
Deferred. Filed so the reasoning survives; not scheduled.

## The problem

`examples/*.ipynb` is committed executed, so every re-execution produces a diff
whether or not anything changed. Two sources, both nondeterministic:

- `iopub.execute_input` / `iopub.status.busy` / `iopub.status.idle` /
  `shell.execute_reply` timestamps in each cell's `execution` metadata.
- The UUIDs xarray mints into the `id='section-...'` and `input id=` attributes
  of its HTML repr, freshly on every render.

Measured on #40: `examples/example_grid_pset.ipynb` came back with a 164-line
diff (82 insertions, 82 deletions) in which **nothing had changed**. Normalising
both revisions by stripping the `execution` metadata and the UUIDs made them
identical, so that file was dropped from the PR. The other four notebooks have
real changes, but their diffs carry the same churn on top.

There is a second cost. `cabo_verde_lcs.ipynb` and
`cabo_verde_lcs_evolution.ipynb` are about 780 kB each, mostly base64 PNG, and
every re-execution rewrites those bytes into the history.

## The direction

Track the notebooks **without** outputs and execute them at docs build time,
i.e. `nb_execution_mode = "auto"` or `"cache"` in `docs/conf.py` instead of the
current `"off"`. The diff then contains only what a human wrote, and the
rendered pages still show real output.

What it costs, and why this is not a five-minute change:

- Read the Docs would need CMEMS credentials and the ~53 MB currents subset
  that `examples/data/` holds, which is gitignored. Today the RTD build needs
  neither, and `.readthedocs.yaml` says so.
- Build time moves from seconds to however long the advections take.
- A build failure becomes a docs failure. Right now a broken example fails
  `test-examples`, which is a clearer signal.
- `AGENTS.md` states the current contract ("the `.ipynb` is committed
  **executed**"), and `examples/README.md` repeats it. Both move with the
  change.
- `myst-nb`'s cache would want somewhere to live that survives an RTD build.

## Cheaper half-measures, if this stays deferred

- `nbconvert --ClearMetadataPreprocessor.enabled=True` with
  `preserve_cell_metadata_mask` set to keep `tags`, which removes the timestamp
  half of the churn and nothing else. The xarray UUIDs have no equivalent lever
  short of a strip filter over the output HTML.
- A `.gitattributes` diff driver, so the churn is hidden in review without
  changing what is stored.

Neither is worth doing on its own if the build-time execution lands.

title: Fix links, canonicalise the PyPI name, clean the notebook outputs
body:
Three link, badge and notebook-output issues in one pass over the public
entry points.

Closes #35
Closes #36
Closes #37

## Links (#36)

The README is the repository front page, the PyPI landing page and, through
`{include}`, the documentation home page. Its five notebook links pointed at
GitHub blob URLs, so the home page of the documentation site sent the reader
off the site to read a notebook the site itself publishes. They now point at
the rendered pages under `examples/`, which resolve the same way in all three
renderings. The pointer to `examples/README.md` moves with them, and the
section's lead-in paragraph goes, so the README points at the site without
restating the jupytext layout, which is developer-facing and already in
`examples/README.md`.

Every link into the documentation names the general URL rather than a redirect
target. Read the Docs serves an unversioned deep link only behind its `/page/`
prefix, checked against the live site: `/page/api.html` resolves and a bare
`/api.html` returns 404. So the root links are
`https://lcs-parcels.readthedocs.io/` and the deep ones take the `/page/` form,
in the README, in `[project.urls]`, and in the Docs badge, which also drops
`?version=latest` and returns a byte-identical SVG without it. The rule is
written down in `AGENTS.md`.

The Scope section linked `docs/api.md` and `docs/numerics.md` by repo path but
sent the reader to the built HTML. The labels now name the pages.

`https://oceanparcels.org/` redirects to `https://parcels-code.org/`, matching
the upstream org rename, and the Copernicus Marine toolbox help link in
`get_data` carried a retired Intercom collection id that redirects to
`9080063-copernicus-marine-toolbox`. Both are written out.

`[project.urls]` gained a `Documentation` entry, which is what puts the
documentation site in the PyPI sidebar; it was absent from the published
2026.8.5.1 metadata. The README gained a prose link to the site beside the
badge. `CHANGELOG.md` is now a page on the site, included rather than copied,
so a reader on Read the Docs can find out what broke in a release.

## The PyPI badge (#35)

The reported symptom does not reproduce. shields.io does normalise the
underscore today: `img.shields.io/pypi/v/lcs_parcels.svg` and
`.../lcs-parcels.svg` both return `pypi: v2026.8.5.1`, checked cache-busted
against the live endpoint, with a known-bad name as a control. So this is a
canonicalisation, not a fix, and no release note claims a broken badge.

The badge, its link target, the `pip install` line and the `pypi` environment
URL in `publish.yml` all use `lcs-parcels` now. `name = "lcs_parcels"` in
`pyproject.toml` is left alone: renaming it churns `pixi.lock` and the pixi
pypi-dependency key for no functional gain, since both spellings already
resolve.

The CI badge gained `?branch=main`. Without it, a red run on any branch or fork
PR shows as a failing badge on the front page and on PyPI while `main` is
green.

## Notebook outputs (#37)

Fixed at the source and re-executed, rather than scrubbed.

`get_data` leaked an absolute path through a `TqdmWarning`, because
`ipywidgets` was not in the `examples` environment. It is now, so the warning
does not fire. Its download cell was also silent whenever the file was already
on disk; it now reports the size in either branch.

The three Cabo Verde notebooks emitted, on the Parcels import cell, an
ipykernel scratch path inside the alpha-version warning and about 55 kB of
holoviews/bokeh bootstrap per notebook. The bootstrap is the worse of the two:
myst-nb inlined its `text/html`, so the published page injected
`cdn.bokeh.org` script tags into the reader's browser and left a dead div,
for a library none of the notebooks use. The import cell is now tagged
`remove-output`, which drops both from the rendered page and leaves the
committed notebook honest. Two of the three needed `cell_metadata_filter:
tags,-all` in their jupytext front matter for the tag to survive a sync.

All five notebooks were re-executed end to end and committed with their
output. A scan of the executed set finds no home path, environment path,
username, credential or error output left anywhere, and a local `-W` build
confirms none of it reaches the rendered pages.

## Release

`CHANGELOG.md` gains a `2026.8.6.1` section, which is what `publish.yml` cuts
the GitHub release from. Nothing in the API changed, so no documented call has
to be rewritten.

## Checks

`pixi run test` (306 passed), `pixi run lint`, `pixi run -e examples
test-examples` (5 passed), `pixi run -e docs docs-build` (`-W`, clean), and
`uv build` plus `twine check --strict` on both artefacts.

## Left out

- A Zenodo DOI and `CITATION.cff`. The badge row has no DOI and the repository
  has no DOI to link to, which needs a call on Zenodo versus a GEOMAR archive,
  and a concept versus per-release DOI.
- A `sphinx-build -b linkcheck` CI job. It would catch the next stale URL, and
  it is also the standard source of flaky red builds.
- `Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only` in the classifiers.
- The Parcels git dependency still names the old `OceanParcels` org, which
  redirects. It moves with the rev bump in #26.
- Re-executing a notebook produces a diff even when nothing changed, from
  execution timestamps and the UUIDs xarray mints into its HTML repr. Deferred
  in #42, which is also where tracking non-executed notebooks is written up.

title: PyPI badge is broken: shields.io does not normalise the underscore
body:
The PyPI badge in `README.md` renders as *"package or version not found"* even
though the package is published.

It is not caching. shields.io does not normalise `_` to `-` in the project name,
and PyPI's canonical name is `lcs-parcels`:

| URL | Result |
|---|---|
| `https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/lcs_parcels.svg` (current) | `pypi: package or version not found` |
| `https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/lcs-parcels.svg` | `pypi: v2026.8.5.1` |

Both checked against the live endpoint.

### Fix

`README.md:3`, one character in the image URL:

```diff
-[![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/lcs_parcels.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/lcs_parcels/)
+[![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/lcs-parcels.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/lcs-parcels/)
```

### Not affected

- The badge's **link target** works either way: `https://pypi.org/project/lcs_parcels/` returns 200, PyPI serves both spellings.
- `.github/workflows/publish.yml:54`'s `url: https://pypi.org/p/lcs_parcels` is the GitHub environment link and resolves fine. Worth making canonical for consistency, but it is not broken.
- `pip install lcs_parcels` is unaffected; pip normalises names itself.

title: Documentation site with Sphinx and MyST (PR 7)
body:
Everything Read the Docs needs except the connection, which only the repository
owner can make. Merging this publishes nothing.

**Structure**, as asked for:

- **Home** — includes `README.md`. Not a copy: the file itself.
- **General docs** — `api`, `notation`, `numerics`, `architecture`, unchanged.
  MyST reads them as they are, so each is the same file on the forge and on the
  site.
- **Examples** — lands on `examples/README.md`, then the five executed
  notebooks, rendered with their committed outputs.
- **API reference** — generated from the docstrings with `autosummary` and
  `autodoc`, grouped as seeds, flow maps and tensor lines.

**Nothing on the site is a maintained second copy.** `docs/examples/` and
`docs/generated/` are produced at build time and gitignored. `conf.py` stages
`examples/README.md` and the `.ipynb` into the source tree, so the README's own
relative links -- which are what make it work on the forge -- resolve on the
site too. A symlink was tried first and does not work: Sphinx resolves it to its
real path and then looks the links up beside the original.

`docs/api.md` stays, retitled **API guide** so it no longer collides with the
generated **API reference**. It is the written document for onboarding a
developer, an agent or an inquisitive user; the generated pages carry the
signatures. Generated output costs no maintenance, so the two are not duplicated
effort.

**Sphinx rather than MkDocs Material**, reversing the choice PR 7 first made and
the plan recorded as contingent. The trigger arrived immediately and for a
stronger reason than the one anticipated: this structure needs three MkDocs
plugins -- `mkdocs-include-markdown-plugin` to reuse the READMEs,
`mkdocs-jupyter` to render the notebooks, `mkdocstrings` for the reference --
on a framework whose next major removes the plugin system, whose 1.x has had no
release in 18 months, and whose theme is steering users to a different tool. All
three are core or first-party in Sphinx: `include`, `myst-nb`, `autodoc`. It is
also what Parcels builds its reference with.

`myst_enable_extensions` includes `dollarmath`, so the `$...$` the documents are
written in renders, and `myst_heading_anchors` keeps the cross-document anchors
working.

**`-W` makes every warning a failure**, so a broken cross-reference or a page
missing from a `toctree` fails the `docs` CI job rather than shipping. The build
is clean: no warnings.

`.readthedocs.yaml` builds through pixi with `--locked`, so the site comes from
the same manifest and lockfile as everything else. A `docs` pixi feature and
environment carry Sphinx, MyST and myst-nb, with `docs-build` and
`docs-serve` tasks.

**Links out of `docs/`.** Six relative links escaped the docs tree, into
`../src/`, `../examples/` and `../plans/`, and would have resolved against the
site. All six are absolute repository URLs now. Two pointed at
`plans/timing-design.md`, archived to `plans/done/` since; they point there.

`AGENTS.md` gains two rules: `docs/` is a built site, so a new page needs a
`toctree` entry and a link out of the tree is absolute; and nothing on the site
is a maintained second copy, with the distinction that duplicated output is free
while duplicated effort is not.

No documentation badge in the README. There is no site to link to until the
project is connected.

**User action, not blocking this merge:** connect the Read the Docs project.

306 tests pass, lint clean, `pixi lock --check` up to date, and the site builds
with warnings as errors.

---

## Review pass: prose, renames, and the review remarks (second commit)

### The six review remarks

- `ci.yml` no longer explains the `docs` job through `mkdocs.yml`'s `strict:
  true`. It says what actually gates it, Sphinx `-W`.
- `conf.py` carries `author = "Henry Owusu Adjei, Willi Rath"` and
  `copyright = "2026, GEOMAR"`.
- `docs/index.md` runs **Examples, then API reference, then General docs**, and
  the example toctree is in increasing scope: `README`, `get_data`,
  `example_grid_pset`, `cabo_verde_ftle`, `cabo_verde_lcs`,
  `cabo_verde_lcs_evolution`. Both READMEs list them in that same order.
- The post-colon teasers are gone from the H1s in the files themselves:
  **API guide**, **Numerics**, **Architecture**.
- The executed notebooks no longer carry progress bars (`verbose_progress=False`
  on every `pset.execute`) or echoed matplotlib artist reprs (`plt.show()` where
  the example already drives matplotlib, `_ =` for the one vanilla
  `.plot.pcolormesh` line). `ruff format` strips a trailing `;`, so that idiom
  could not be used. 65 progress-bar streams and 4 artist reprs removed.
- Both READMEs now point at `get_data`.

### The prose pass

All ~70 inline `TODO` comments are resolved. The dominant finding was volume:
26 of them said "condense". Every numeric paragraph that was cut already existed
in `docs/numerics.md`, in fuller form, so this is deletion of a second copy
rather than a migration.

`AGENTS.md` gains six rules generalised from the comments: a **length budget**
stated as a number (three lines per docstring paragraph, two per comment), a
**destination test** for any sentence about *why*, **working correctly is not a
feature** (the antimeridian was documented in four docstrings), **punctuation**
(call-out colons, `--` asides, semicolons joining independent clauses), **no
downward or lateral references** (a base class naming its subclasses), and
**local names match the data names they hold**.

### Breaking changes

- `Seed` → `SeedGrid`, `NeighborSeed` → `NeighborSeedGrid`, `AuxiliarySeed` →
  `AuxiliarySeedGrid`.
- `FlowMap.image(lon0=, lat0=)` → `image(lon_0=, lat_0=)`, matching the coords it
  returns.

These need release notes in PR 5's `CHANGELOG.md`.

### Code changes, and what an adversarial pass made of them

- `ftle_ridge_seeds` picks its seeds with `stack`/`where(drop=True)` instead of
  `transpose(...).values[mask]`. **Bit-identical** across empty selection, full
  selection, NaN fields, non-square and transposed grids. One narrow difference:
  `where()` upcasts integer coords to float, unreachable through the package's
  own API since both seed grids always produce `float64`.
- `_grid_summary` is gone; `SeedGrid` and `FlowMap` each carry a complete
  `__repr__` rather than sharing a helper that returned an unclosed `<...` for
  both callers to close. **Byte-identical** reprs, including all-NaN grids, 1x1,
  backward `T`, sub-day windows and `.005` rounding boundaries.
- The `cauchy_green` rename/`assign_coords` reorder is **bit-identical** across
  26 configurations, on name, dims, attrs, coord order and raw bit patterns.
- `_DEG` → `_M_PER_DEG` plus `np.deg2rad` is **not** bit-preserving, and the PR
  says so. The constant is parenthesised to match the old value exactly; what
  remains is re-association inside `_separation_m`, worth at most 3 ULP on a
  separation and 8.9e-13 relative on the FTLE. No test tolerance comes within
  68x of its budget, `_odd_cells`' `round()` never lands within 0.0083 of a
  `.5` boundary, and seed selection was unchanged in every configuration
  measured.

The same pass found seven prose statements the condensation had made false:
"any input convention works", "a traced line may run anywhere", a dropped
strict-maxima caveat that a passing test contradicted, `_odd_cells` "rounding
down", `line_length_m` as a cap, a lost arm NaN-ing "the whole grid point", and
a reference to the deleted `_grid_summary`. All seven are fixed in the last
commit.

Gate: `ruff` clean, 306 unit tests, 5 example tests, cold `-W` docs build clean.
Notebooks re-executed and re-synced.

### Em-dashes

211 em-dashes and 51 ASCII `--` asides are gone from the docs, the README, the
plans in flight, `AGENTS.md`, the examples and the tests. Each was rewritten
rather than swapped for another character: an aside becomes a comma clause, a
parenthesis, or its own sentence.

Left alone deliberately: en-dashes in compound names (`Cauchy–Green`,
`east–west`, all 43 of them), which are correct typography rather than the tic;
`| — |` table cells meaning "not applicable", which became empty cells; and the
definition dash on first use, which the review accepted.



---

Part of #12: the Read the Docs page. The remaining items on that issue (the PyPI
release and its badges) are PR 5, which closes it.

title: Release v2026.8.5.1: publish workflow, changelog, tag-derived version (PR 5)
body:
Everything the first PyPI release needs. **Merging this publishes nothing** —
only pushing the `v2026.8.5.1` tag does, and that is a separate deliberate act.

**`.github/workflows/publish.yml`.** Triggered on a `v*` tag. Builds, checks, and
uploads with PyPI Trusted Publishing over OIDC, so there is no API token in the
repository secrets to leak or rotate. Three jobs:

- `build` refuses to go on unless the tag matches `[project] version` and an
  sdist by that exact name exists. A tag and a package version that disagree
  would publish under a name nobody asked for, and PyPI takes a version exactly
  once. Verified locally: `v2026.8.5.1` passes, `v2026.08.05.1` and
  `v2026.8.5.2` are both refused.
- `publish` runs in a `pypi` environment, which is also where a required
  approval can be attached.
- `release` cuts the GitHub release with the `CHANGELOG.md` section for that
  version as its body, and fails if there is no such section, so the file and the
  release cannot drift.

**`CHANGELOG.md`.** New. The loosened compatibility rule in `AGENTS.md` says a
release that breaks a documented call states what broke and what to write
instead; this is where that lives. The `2026.8.5.1` section lists five breaking
changes from PRs 1 and 2 — the `ftle_ridge_seeds` return type above all — with
the replacement call written out.

**Version.** `2026.8.5.1` in `pyproject.toml` and `__init__.py`, unpadded per the
CalVer rule. `test_version_matches_the_installed_distribution` covers the pair.

**README.** `pip install lcs_parcels` becomes the primary instruction, the
`git+https://` form stays for unreleased `main`, and a PyPI version badge is
added.

This last part is the plan's PR 6, folded in deliberately. The plan sequenced it
after the release because `pip install lcs_parcels` only resolves once the name
is on PyPI. But the README is embedded verbatim in the sdist and the wheel, so
whatever it says at tag time is the PyPI landing page for that version,
permanently. Leaving PR 6 separate would publish a page reading "There is no
release on PyPI yet." The cost of folding it in is that `main` claims a release
that does not exist for as long as it takes to push the tag.

**Blocking, and only you can do it:** a pending publisher for `lcs_parcels` has
to exist on pypi.org before the tag is pushed. Publisher settings: owner
`geomar-od-lagrange`, repository `lcs_parcels`, workflow `publish.yml`,
environment `pypi`.

306 tests pass, lint clean, `twine check --strict` passes on both artefacts, and
the sdist carries `CHANGELOG.md`.

Closes #12.


---

**Versioning changed while this PR was open.** The version is no longer written
in `pyproject.toml` and `__init__.py` and bumped by hand. `hatch-vcs` derives it
from the git tag, `__version__` reads it back off the installed distribution,
and releasing is just tagging. `publish.yml` lost the tag-vs-version comparison
and the PEP 440 normalisation check along with it, keeping a three-line guard
that the built sdist matches the tag before the upload.

Tested by building at a temporary local `v2026.8.5.1` tag: a clean tree gives
`lcs_parcels-2026.8.5.1.tar.gz` and the matching wheel. A *dirty* tree at the
same tag gives `2026.8.5.2.dev0+g...d20260805` instead, which is what that guard
is there to stop reaching PyPI.

title: Packaging metadata, Python matrix, coverage gate and Dependabot (PR 4)
body:
The bulk of issue #12. Everything needed to publish, without publishing: the
version is not bumped and no tag is pushed. PR 5 is the release.

**Metadata.** `authors` (Henry Adjei, Willi Rath) and `maintainers`, keywords,
classifiers, `[project.urls]`, and PEP 639 `license = "MIT"` with
`license-files` in place of the old `license = { file = "LICENSE" }`, which put
the whole MIT text into the `License:` field. The build already emitted
Metadata 2.4, which takes the SPDX form.

**Dependency floors.** `numpy>=2.1`, `xarray>=2024.9`, `scipy>=1.15`, each the
SPEC 0 line — the oldest minor released inside the 24-month window — with the
dates recorded beside them. Floors only, no caps: a cap in a library's metadata
propagates into every downstream resolution. A new `minimum-dependencies` CI job
installs with `uv --resolution lowest-direct` and runs the suite, so a wrong
floor fails there instead of in a user's environment.

**Python range.** `requires-python = ">=3.12"`, replacing an untested `>=3.11`.
pixi features `py312`/`py313`/`py314` pin nothing but an interpreter; `default`
takes `py313` so it agrees with `examples`. CI adds an ubuntu job for each end of
the range. 306 tests pass on 3.12.13, 3.13.14 and 3.14.6.

**Coverage.** `pytest-cov`, a `test-cov` task and a CI job, gated at
`--cov-fail-under=100` with the three `raise NotImplementedError` bodies
excluded. Currently 100% statement and 100% branch over 288 statements. No badge
and no third-party service: the gate is the whole mechanism.

**sdist.** Excludes `.claude`, `.github`, `.gitattributes`, `AGENTS.md`,
`CLAUDE.md`, `pixi.lock`, `plans` and `*.ipynb`. The executed notebooks were 85%
of a 1.0 MB archive and their value is that they render on the forge, which an
sdist does not; the `.py` they are generated from stay, so the example tests
still have something to run. 1.0 MB to 108 KB.

**Dependabot.** `github-actions` only — not a scoping decision but the whole of
what it can see: there is no pixi ecosystem, its pip ecosystem does not read
`[tool.pixi.*]`, and the `[project]` dependencies carry floors and no caps.

**README.** CI and license badges, and a `pip install git+https://...` line so
users are not forced through pixi before PyPI exists.

**What adversarial verification changed.** Six of these were wrong when first
written:

title: Prose pass against the short-factual-statements rule (PR 3)
body:
Reads every line of reader-facing prose in the repository against `AGENTS.md`'s
rule — "short factual statements, never an aphoristic tone" — and rewrites what
fails it. Prose only: no behaviour change, no rename, no signature change, and
no number, threshold or measured value altered.

About 130 passages across `README.md`, all five files in `docs/`, the docstrings
and comments in `src/lcs_parcels/`, the markdown cells of the five example
notebooks, `examples/README.md` and `AGENTS.md` itself.

**Second standard.** The English is also gauged against NASA **KSC-DF-107
Revision F**, the Kennedy Space Center Technical Documentation Style Guide
(2017-07-08), fetched from NASA's public standards site rather than recalled.
Sections 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.6, 3.7, 3.8, 3.10, 3.11 and Appendix A apply; the
formal-document half of the guide — cover pages, `shall`/`will` requirements
language, title case, figure numbering — does not, since a Python package with
Markdown docs is not a NASA deliverable. Where the two standards conflict,
`AGENTS.md` wins.

The two agree closely. §3.1 is the positive form of the house rule: "If you think
the sentences don't sound important enough, you're probably on the right track."
What KSC-DF-107 added beyond it:

- **§3.8.1**, attributive-noun stacks capped at three. No run of four or more
  survives in prose or a heading; the one that remains is a `long_name` value,
  which is API surface and out of scope.
- **§3.2**, one concept one name. Eight terms had drifted: window vs
  neighbourhood, seed point vs start point, well-definedness guard vs degeneracy
  guard, metres vs meters inside one file, neighbouring vs neighboring, modelled
  vs modeled, diagnostic grid vs analysis grid, window vs horizon.
- **§3.11**, parallel construction. The stencil bullets in `architecture.md` and
  `notation.md` described the same pair with different labels and different parts
  of speech.
- **§3.7**, pronouns with a clear antecedent. Three fixed, including one sentence
  where two adjacent `it`s referred to different things.
- **Appendix A**, `e.g.` and `i.e.` take a following comma. Nine sites.

Also swept, as issue #25 asks: no unicode math glyph remains in `README.md`,
`docs/`, `src/` or the example sources, and every citation carries a DOI.

**What adversarial review caught, and what it says about a prose pass.** Making a
sentence clearer is a good way to make it untrue. Four claims were strengthened
past what the code does and are restored here:

- `architecture.md` said `hyperbolic_lcs()` hands the FTLE field to both steps
  below it. It goes to the ridge finder only; `shrink_lines` takes the flow map.
- `tensorlines.py` and `numerics.md` said the tensor-line step stays on a
  direction field "exactly, at any step size and any latitude". Measured: exact
  for a field aligned with a parallel or a meridian, but a midpoint rule on any
  other heading — 0.04 m at 60 N on a 45-degree heading at a 25 km step, 2.6 m at
  100 km. Stated that way now.
- `grid_image` attributed the reference stencil separation to the *advected*
  arms, which have moved.
- The evolution example said the same map that diagnosed a curve also moves it.
  The notebook does the opposite: each family is diagnosed on one direction and
  evolved by the maps of the other, as a later cell in the same file states.

Three hedges were also restored: `numerics.md`'s auxiliary-arm accuracy holds
away from the pole (the zonal limit falls to 1 km itself only above about 88 N),
`grids.py`'s finite-difference term dominates on a coarse grid, and
`AGENTS.md`'s notebook cross-reference rule bans *mutual* reference between
same-rank examples rather than all reference.

**Notebooks.** All five `.py` sources were edited, so all five triplets are
re-synced with `jupytext --sync` and the `.ipynb` re-executed against CMEMS. Two
run-dependent claims were verified against the real run rather than assumed:
the Cabo Verde FTLE is 0.098/day median with a 10.2-day e-folding time ("around
0.1/day, about ten days"), and 28% of repelling and 24% of attracting seeds trace
no curve ("about a quarter").

**One deliberate deletion.** `AGENTS.md` loses "An example that no longer matches
the code is worse than no example." It is the balanced comparison the rule bans,
and the surviving "a broken or stale example is treated like a failing test, not
a TODO" carries the operational force.

305 tests pass, lint clean, all five examples execute.

Closes #25

title: Report what `window_m` implies, and add an absolute ridge floor (PR 2)
body:
Closes #21 and #22. Both touch the `ftle_ridge_seeds` signature, so it changes
once.

**#21 — `window_m` keeps its meaning; its consequences are now reported.**
`window_m` stays the *side* of the neighbourhood, so two seeds can be about
`window_m / 2` apart. Redefining it as the minimum seed separation was rejected:
a redefined float is a break that does not fail, and every existing call would
keep running with a knob that means something else.

Instead `ftle_ridge_seeds` returns the numbers. `_window_cells` becomes
`_window_geometry`, and the returned dataset carries `window_m`, the odd
per-dimension cell counts, the median grid spacings those came from, and
`min_seed_separation_m` — the closest two seeds can be, on this grid. In the
Cabo Verde example a 30 km window reports 16 872 m, which is the confusion the
issue is about.

It also warns when `window_m` spans fewer than three cells in either dimension.
A one-cell window makes every point a windowed maximum, so the local-maximum
test stops selecting and only the magnitude floor is left, silently.

**#22 — an absolute floor is available; the quantile stays the default.**
`ftle_min` sets the floor as an absolute value in the field's own units.
`quantile` and `ftle_min` are mutually exclusive and passing both raises; passing
neither is `quantile=0.90`, exactly as before.

`ftle_min` is deliberately not scale-free, which `AGENTS.md` otherwise requires.
The carve-out is written down there: the rule governs what a knob *defaults* to,
and a non-scale-free parameter is allowed opt-in beside a scale-free default when
an analysis needs exactly that. Comparing runs across windows or regions needs
one threshold for all of them, and a per-field quantile cannot express one.

**Return type.** `ftle_ridge_seeds` returned a `(lon, lat)` tuple of arrays and
now returns an `xr.Dataset` — `lon`/`lat` on a `seed` dim, each with `long_name`
and `units`, and the metadata above in `attrs`. Call sites read
`shrink_lines(fm, seed_lon=seeds["lon"], seed_lat=seeds["lat"])`.
`FlowMap.hyperbolic_lcs` gained `ftle_min`, and the ridge-selection attrs ride
along on what it returns.

**One defect found by adversarial review and fixed here.** The first
`min_seed_separation_m` multiplied the *median* cell size, which is not a bound:
the window is a count of cells and cells converge poleward, so seeds at the
poleward end of a grid sit closer than the number claimed. Measured violated by
11% over a 30-degree latitude band and by a factor of 3 over 75. It now uses the
grid's smallest cell, and the test is parametrized over five latitude bands where
the bound is attained rather than merely respected. It bounds *strict* maxima; a
plateau of exactly equal values ties at every one of its cells, which is now an
asserted, documented behaviour.

**Also.** The `get-data` pixi task ran from the repository root while
`examples/get_data.py` writes to `data/` relative to the working directory, so it
dropped a 52 MB CMEMS file at the root, outside the `examples/data/` gitignore
and contradicting the task's own description. It now runs with `cwd = "examples"`,
matching `tests/test_examples.py`.

305 tests pass, no warnings. `examples/cabo_verde_lcs` is re-executed against
CMEMS and all five examples pass.

Closes #21
Closes #22

title: Per-point local metric frame and wrap-aware longitudes (PR 1)
body:
Replaces the equirectangular metres frame with a single standard parallel by a
per-point local east/north frame, and makes every longitude difference and mean
wrap. Both were designed together, as #18 asked.

**Metric.** `_separation_m` measures each pair in its own local frame: the
longitude difference scaled by the cosine of the pair's mid-latitude, the
latitude difference by the Earth radius. There is no shared projection left, so
`grad F` is the true tangent-space Jacobian and a rigid meridional translation
reports the stretching it actually causes instead of zero. `AuxiliarySeed` lays
its arms with each grid point's own cosine, so an arm span is exactly `2s`
everywhere rather than only at the grid centroid.

The mid-latitude cosine is a midpoint rule, so accuracy is set by the separation
of the pair and its latitude, not by the size of the domain: the zonal relative
error is `(dlambda sin(phi))**2 / 24`, crossing 1e-6 at `31.2 km / tan(phi)`.
The docs state that number rather than claiming the frame is exact.

**Longitudes.** Nothing is normalised on ingest — whatever convention you hand in
is what you get back. Only differences and means wrap. `_wrap_lon` subtracts the
nearest multiple of 360, so a difference already inside the range is unchanged
bit-for-bit. The auxiliary centroid averages on the circle.

**Tensor-line stepping.** The step is now the exact inverse of `_separation_m`.
A great-circle arc leaves a heading-invariant direction field at
`(step/R)**2 tan(phi) / 2` per step, which accumulates *linearly* in the step
count: a due-east field at 70 N drifts 3.4 km off its parallel over an 800 km
line at a 20 km step, and halving the step only halves it. The inverse step
leaves it exactly, measured at 0.0 m at 0, 45 and 70 N at every step size.

**Two defects found by adversarial review and fixed here.** `FlowMap.image`
interpolated advected longitudes with no wrap handling, so an advection
returning positions wrapped to `[-180, 180)` — which is what Parcels and CMEMS
do — tore between adjacent grid points and the linear interpolant read the tear
as a 40 000 km jump; the images are now re-anchored on their grid point's
branch. And `AuxiliarySeed` aliased through the wrap into an arm on the far side
of the pole, returning a wrong gradient rather than a NaN; that is now a
`ValueError`.

**Tests.** The shared axis fixtures are parametrized over three regions —
`reference`, `antimeridian` and `high_latitude` — so every operator, grid and
tensor-line test runs where the change bites. The synthetic advection returns
its longitudes wrapped, as Parcels does, which is what makes the antimeridian
region exercise the branch cut: neutering `_wrap_lon` to the identity fails 16
tests, 9 of them `[antimeridian]`-parametrized. 113 tests became 285.

On a sphere no map has a constant tangent Jacobian, so the old premise that a
constant linear `M` gives `grad F == M` everywhere is gone. `conftest` now
carries the closed-form expectation instead: the flat-frame Jacobian rescaled by
`diag(cos(Phi), 1) . J . diag(1/cos(phi), 1)`, which is exactly the correction
#18 proposed. Both stencils match it to 1.5e-14 (neighbour) and 3.0e-12
(auxiliary) across all three regions.

**Remaining restriction**, now stated in the README rather than as an open
issue: `FlowMap.image` and the tensor-line functions interpolate along the
`lon_grid` axis, so it must be monotonic. A domain crossing the antimeridian is
seeded `170, 175, 180, 185`, not `170, 175, 180, -175`.

Closes #18
Closes #13

title: Prepare for publishing to PyPI
body:
Sequences #12, #13, #18, #21, #22 and #25 into seven PRs, ordered by the three
constraints that force a split: install instructions need a package that exists,
the publish workflow needs a release that runs it, and an RTD link needs a site
that builds.

Records what was measured at 2c71ccb: the PyPI name is free, the build is clean,
coverage is 99% statement and branch with the three misses all abstract-method
bodies, PEP 440 normalises `2026.08.04.1` to `2026.8.4.1`, and the sdist ships
`.claude/` and `plans/`. The published name is `lcs_parcels`, matching the
import; PyPI normalises it to `lcs-parcels` in index URLs, so the hyphen form
resolves to the same project.

## Two `AGENTS.md` rules change here

Publishing invalidates their premise, and they govern the PRs that follow, so
they are settled before those start rather than inside one of them.

- Breaking changes are the norm, and backward compatibility that complicates the
  code is never kept — no shims, no aliases, no legacy branches. This is
  research-grade alpha code. What publishing changes is only that a break now
  reaches people who did not read the PR that made it, so it goes in that
  version's release notes.
- Supported versions follow [SPEC 0](https://scientific-python.org/specs/spec-0000/),
  so the window moves on a published schedule. Applied on 2026-08-04 that gives
  Python 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14 — 3.11's drop date was 2025-10-23, and 3.14 has
  been out since 2025-10-07 and is currently tested nowhere. The suite passes on
  3.14 unmodified.

## The dependency floors are settled, and one fix is committed

Working the floors out during planning turned up a real defect, so this is not
deferred to PR 4. Floors are `numpy>=2.2`, `scipy>=1.15`, `xarray>=2024.9`, all
straight from SPEC 0's two-year window with no exception to carry.

The xarray floor first measured at 2025.11, nine releases above the policy line.
Everything from 2023.12 to 2025.10 failed the same three metadata tests, because
`xr.dot` returns the coordinates it carried through stripped of their attrs
before 2025.11 — so `i` came back with no `long_name` and output metadata stopped
being the axis label. Probed one operation at a time: `apply_ufunc`, `concat`,
`broadcast`, `where`, `isel` and arithmetic all preserve attrs on every version
tested; `xr.dot` alone does not. We call it once, in `cauchy_green`.

`cauchy_green` now restores those attrs from the operand after the contraction.
`xr.dot` itself stays: it names the operation, the tensor is 2x2 so nothing here
is on a hot path, and it does not skip NaN — a rewrite to `.sum()` did, and
silently summed a lost particle as zero until `test_nan_propagates_through_chain`
caught it. That discarded version is still in the branch history.

The restore reads its coordinate list from the operand rather than naming
entries. Measured on 2024.9, `xr.dot` strips `i`, `j`, `lon_grid`, `lat_grid`,
`t0` and `T`; naming `i` and `j` would have missed four, since `assert_labelled`
stops at the first failure and never reported the rest.

Suite passes at xarray 2024.9, 2025.1, 2025.10 and 2026.1, and 103 pass on the
current stack. Lint clean.

## Open decisions

Marked in the plan, each needed before the PR it belongs to: the longitude
branch-cut convention and whether the metric frame becomes per-point local
east/north (PR 1), whether `window_m` is redefined as the seed separation and
whether ridge selection keeps `quantile` as its default (PR 2), and MkDocs
Material against Sphinx with MyST (PR 7).

title: Parcels A-grid interpolation is wrong when particles do not share one clock
body:
Findings from diagnosing why `examples/cabo_verde_lcs_evolution` could not reuse
one integration across horizons. Written up here so the analysis survives;
**not reported to OceanParcels/Parcels** — decide separately whether and how to
file it there.

Parcels is the pinned v4 alpha
(`rev = 5a0df965fe70f37add860230cbcd3b2fc03ffd2e`). Line numbers are into that
build, under `.pixi/envs/examples/lib/python3.13/site-packages/parcels/`.

## The bug

`interpolators/_xinterpolators.py::_get_corner_data_Agrid` builds its corner
index arrays in two incompatible orderings:

```
:34   ti = np.repeat(ti, lenZ * 4)                                       # particle-major
:41   zi = np.repeat(zi, lenT * 4)                                       # particle-major
:48   yi = np.tile(np.array([yi, yi, yi_1, yi_1]).flatten(), lenT*lenZ)  # corner-major
:52   xi = np.tile(np.array([xi, xi_1]).flatten(), lenT*lenZ*2)          # corner-major
:65   return data.isel(...).reshape(lenT, lenZ, 2, 2, npart)             # corner-major
```

The `np.repeat` calls should be `np.tile`. As written, particle `p` is
interpolated from the time (and depth) index belonging to particle
`floor((c * npart + p) / 4)`.

This is invisible while every particle in the set shares one time index — the
assumption Parcels states in `_core/_windowed_array.py:6-8` ("all particles
share the clock"). Where that does not hold it returns silently wrong values
rather than raising.

The same `repeat`/reshape mismatch appears in `CGrid_Velocity` (`:227`, `:230`,
`:241`) and `CGrid_Tracer` (`:370-373`). Only the A-grid path was exercised
here; the C-grid ones are **unverified**.

`XLinear_Velocity` is what CMEMS A-grid velocities resolve to
(`_core/model.py:169`), so this is the default path for the examples in this
repository.

## The headline case: staggered release times

No error handling is involved, and nothing goes wrong in the run. Four
open-ocean particles, no land nearby, no recovery kernel, every particle
finishing in `Success`. The only difference between the two runs is when the
*other three* particles are released:

```python
# A: every particle on the same clock
ParticleSet(..., t=[t0, t0,    t0,    t0   ]); execute(dt=1h, endtime=t0+24h)
# B: particle 0 identical, its batch-mates released 3 h later
ParticleSet(..., t=[t0, t0+3h, t0+3h, t0+3h]); execute(dt=1h, endtime=t0+24h)
```

Particle 0 starts at the same place and time and integrates the same 24 h in
both runs, and ends **1237.8 m** away from itself:

```
particle 0, uniform clock  : -24.101357  16.006674
particle 0, staggered mates: -24.103165  16.017677
```

A particle's trajectory depends on when unrelated particles in the same set were
released.

This is the severe form, because staggered release is a first-class Parcels
feature — `ParticleSet` accepts a per-particle `t` array — and continuous or
rolling release is an ordinary Lagrangian workflow. It is also the pattern this
repository's own `AGENTS.md` documents (`ParticleSet(..., t=t0_array)`): a
uniform `t0_array` is safe, a genuinely staggered one is silently wrong.

## The second case: restarting a particle set

1. A particle that errors is skipped by `Kernel._position_update`
   (`_core/kernel.py:222-224`), so its `t` freezes at the moment it was lost.
2. A recovery kernel parks it at `StatusCode.EndofLoop`, as `AGENTS.md`
   requires. Within a single `execute` it then stays out of the batch and the
   clock remains uniform — so `EndofLoop` is exact for single-`execute` use, and
   the other Cabo Verde notebooks are unaffected.
3. `_core/kernel.py:190` resets **every** particle to `StatusCode.Evaluate` at
   the start of each `execute`. A second `execute` on the same set therefore
   returns stale-`t` particles to the batch, the clock is no longer uniform, and
   the surviving particles are interpolated from the wrong time level.

So the recovery kernel is not at fault; reusing a particle set whose clock has
already fractured is.

## Evidence

- A single open-ocean particle is bit-identical between one 3-day integration
  and three checkpointed 1-day legs — 0.000 m, both directions, with and without
  a recovery kernel. Every step is 3600 s; nothing is cropped. Not a stepping or
  timestep-cropping difference.
- Restricted to particles that never go NaN, or on a grid with no land, reused
  and fresh sets agree bit-for-bit. The lost particles are the coupling.
- Monkey-patching the four `np.repeat` to `np.tile` drives the difference to
  exactly 0 at every horizon while leaving the per-horizon result bit-unchanged,
  which identifies the cause and shows which of the two is correct.
- Error-handler comparison on a land-straddling grid, reused set vs fresh runs:

  | handler | day 1 | day 2 | day 3 |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `EndofLoop` | 0 differ | 249 differ, 600 m | 308 differ, 1260 m |
  | `Evaluate` | 0 | 0 | 0 |

At 1/25 degree (19026 particles), a reused set was wrong for 1668 particles by
day 2 and 2971 (16%) by day 5, up to 3460 m, clustered near the land mask —
which is where FTLE ridges are diagnosed.

## What we did

`examples/cabo_verde_lcs_evolution.py` reaches the horizons one leg at a time
and builds a **new** `ParticleSet` for each leg, from the previous leg's end
positions, released at that leg's start time. Every particle is on one clock by
construction, so the precondition holds regardless of what upstream does.

Verified bit-identical to integrating each horizon from scratch: 0 particles
differ at any horizon on the test grid, and at the notebook's resolution the NaN
counts are 444, 564, 717, 812, 903 forward — matching the per-horizon run
exactly, including the 717 and 903 that a reused set got wrong as 716 and 902.
Cost is 5 particle-days per direction instead of 15.

## Rejected

- **`StatusCode.Evaluate` in the recovery kernel.** Keeps lost particles'
  clocks advancing and is bit-identical (table above), but it contradicts the
  recovery-kernel convention in `AGENTS.md`, wastes an RK4 evaluation per dead
  particle per step, and is correct only by virtue of the upstream precondition
  rather than by maintaining it.
- **`StatusCode.Delete`.** Keeps the clock uniform, but shrinks the particle
  array and breaks alignment with the seed order — already ruled out in
  `AGENTS.md`.

## If this goes upstream

Two independent fixes, worth mentioning separately:

1. `np.repeat` → `np.tile` in the four index constructions, plus the same review
   for the C-grid interpolators.
2. Check the precondition. `_windowed_array.py:6-8` asserts the shared clock in
   prose and nothing enforces it. Raising on a non-uniform clock would have
   turned this into an immediate failure instead of a 16%-wrong result that runs
   clean — and would be worth having even after the ordering is fixed.

title: Full prose pass against the short-factual-statements rule
body:
`AGENTS.md` gained a prose rule in PR C (#24): short factual statements, never an
aphoristic tone — if it sounds like it could be from *The Road Not Taken*, it is
wrong.

The rule was added in response to review comments on #24, and the passages the
review actually pointed at were fixed there. But the review flagged each class of
issue once, at the first place it hit, so the rule has never been applied
repo-wide. That sweep is deliberately **not** folded into #24.

## What this is

Read the reader-facing prose across the repository against the rule and rewrite
what fails it. Not a rewrite for its own sake: the target is sentences that reach
for a resonant closing clause, a balanced pair of opposites, or a formulation
that lands rather than informs.

Candidates, in rough order of likely density:

- `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/numerics.md` — both carry relocated design
  rationale, written to be read rather than used.
- `docs/notation.md`, `docs/api.md`.
- Module and function docstrings in `src/lcs_parcels/`, particularly the
  `grids.py` module docstring and the longer method docstrings in
  `tensorlines.py`.
- The markdown cells of the five example notebooks. Their `.py` is the source of
  truth; edit that, then `jupytext --sync`, then re-execute (a prose-only change
  preserves outputs, but confirm rather than assume).
- `README.md`, `examples/README.md`, `AGENTS.md` itself.

## Constraints

- Prose-only. No behaviour changes, no renames, no signature changes — if a
  passage is wrong rather than merely florid, that is a separate fix.
- The audience model in `AGENTS.md` still decides *what* belongs in each file;
  this issue is only about *how* it is written.
- Notebook `.ipynb` files must stay committed executed. Re-execute anything whose
  cells change and confirm outputs survive.
- Related rules that a pass should enforce at the same time, since they are cheap
  to check while reading every line anyway: LaTeX rather than unicode math in
  Markdown, and a DOI on every citation.

title: Prose, examples, and CI gating (PR C)
body:
Steps 0 and 9-11 of `plans/review-followup.md`, plus the review of this PR.

**#19 is settled as keep.** An investigate-then-refute pass found the case for
renaming final products to plain `lon`/`lat` does not survive. `lon_grid`/`lat_grid`
are 2-D non-dimension coordinates either way, so `.plot()` labels them identically
and the `x=`/`y=` keyword survives a rename; and `hyperbolic_lcs` merges shrink
lines with the FTLE field, which a rename turns into a `MergeError`. The issue's
real complaint was the axis label, fixed by shortening `long_name` to "longitude".

**`docs/architecture.md` is split (#23)** into structure/decisions plus a new
`docs/numerics.md` carrying the shrink-line guard, the metres-frame error analysis
and the tuning-parameter units. Both mermaid diagrams are gone.

**Prose hygiene.** The design document at the top of `grids.py` relocates into the
split docs rather than being deleted; `__init__.py` loses its meta-comment;
`docs/notation.md` loses its history of this repository. The dangling `plans/done/`
links in `src/` and `tests/` are gone, so AGENTS.md's claim that neither links to
plans is now true.

**Examples rewritten** for the inquisitive user: `set_lost_to_nan` written out in
each advecting notebook rather than shared, single-use helpers dissolved, the
datasets displayed, both stencils shown, round-trip demos and contract framing
dropped, the hand-written `* 86400.0` conversions gone now that PR B put units on
everything returned, vanilla plots throughout. `example_grid_pset` advects nothing
at all -- $u = v = 0$ over ten days, so the FTLE is exactly zero and the only thing
separating the two stencils is coverage.

**The data story is download-once.** A new `examples/get_data` notebook fetches the
CMEMS subset to `examples/data/` (gitignored, never committed) and skips the
download when it is already there. A fresh clone can run all five notebooks;
previously three of four failed with no way to obtain the data.

**Examples are gated as tests.** `tests/test_examples.py` executes each `.py`
source as a script -- `# %%` is a comment, so the jupytext source is already the
executable artifact and no notebook machinery is needed. One test per example, so
a failure names the notebook that broke. Selection is by marker: `pixi run test`
takes the unit suite plus the credential-free example on all three platforms, and
the `examples` job runs all five. CI caches the 52 MB subset keyed on
`get_data.py`. This replaces a per-notebook pixi task graph: pixi stays an
environment manager with flat entry points, and the orchestration lives in pytest,
which makes AGENTS.md's "a broken example is treated like a failing test" literally
true.

**Acting on the review.** All 50 inline comments, plus the further instances of
each that the review stopped short of after flagging the first. The substantive
ones:

- The ridge-window argument was inverted. `ftle_ridge_seeds` rolls a full-width
  window, so two seeds cannot be closer than about `window_m / 2`: we want ~15 km
  separation, which is *why* the window is 30 km. The docstring said "spanning
  `window_m` in each direction", the same error, and now states the implied
  minimum spacing.
- attracting/repelling leaves `FlowMap`. A flow map is integrated one way or the
  other and knows nothing more; which LCS family that yields belongs to the
  diagnostic. `_direction()` becomes `_time_direction()` returning
  `forward`/`backward`, with the duality applied in `hyperbolic_lcs`.
- `cabo_verde_lcs_evolution` reaches its horizons one leg at a time instead of
  restarting from $t_0$ for each, building a fresh `ParticleSet` per leg so every
  particle stays on one clock. Reusing a set across legs is *not* equivalent --
  it trips an upstream Parcels interpolation bug (#26) and was wrong for 16% of
  particles by up to 3.5 km, concentrated near the land mask where the ridges
  are. The per-leg form is verified bit-identical to integrating each horizon
  separately.
- `T0`/`T1` collided with the signed window `T` and become
  `RELEASE_TIME`/`END_TIME`; `lead` becomes the sign-neutral `offset`;
  `attracting`/`repelling` become `attracting_lcs`/`repelling_lcs`.
- The official CMEMS product `GLOBAL_ANALYSISFORECAST_PHY_001_024`
  ([doi:10.48670/moi-00016](https://doi.org/10.48670/moi-00016)) is named in
  `get_data`, and AGENTS.md gains the prose rule the review proposed.

The example suite runs in 33s, from 486s at the start of this PR. Most of that is
eager-loading the currents rather than reading them lazily per RK4 substep; the
rest is not re-integrating the early horizons.

Filed rather than folded in: #25 (a full prose pass against the new rule) and #26
(the Parcels interpolation bug, with the analysis and a reproducer).
